modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

plans.name: Current applicable tariff unverified
plans.note: Usage-based: pay per successful task (job) execution; development/teaching is included. No public price: no pricing page (minicor.com/pricing 404), sales via 'Book a demo'. Not a per-VM-hour tariff: Minicor-provisioned cloud Windows desktops or customer-owned machines/VPC/on-prem.

caveats: Public enterprise desktop-automation product; YC explicitly says scalable Windows desktop automation/VM. Quote-led offering, no verified Windows CPU/RAM/license-inclusive tariff. Product website sign-in/demo does not prove self-serve availability.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

own_agent_api.quote: `publish_job`, `get_build_status`, `answer_build_question`, `cancel_build`: go live, follow the builder, answer its questions.
own_agent_api.note: Only Minicor's own builder agent (teach_job starts it from a description plus a sample; follow status, answer its questions, cancel) via the Minicor MCP (hosted https://mcp.minicor.com/mcp) and the co-pilot. The builder runs in Minicor's platform and drives the Windows desktop; live jobs are deterministic code triggered by one HTTP call. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosting. The MCP also lets you 'create and manage on-demand, scheduled, or monitoring agents'.

secret_proxy.quote: Key-value settings resolved into a job at run time. Credentials live here, not in the automation.
secret_proxy.note: Credential vault ('Configurations') plus 2FA/OTP secrets referenced by ID; values are resolved into the run and typed into the target desktop app on the VM, so they do reach the machine. No outbound-request credential-injection proxy.
